HNSW-guided repair narrows the exact-evaluation set
Approximate retrieval finds plausible insertion positions first; exact routing checks begin only after feasibility has reduced the search.
HERO retrieves candidate positions first, filters feasibility second, and evaluates only the surviving set exactly.
Query — Build a feature query for the removed customer.
Candidate pool — Combine HNSW neighbors with positions from geographically close routes.
Feasibility filter — Retain candidates passing capacity and time-window checks.
Commit and refresh — Insert the selected customer, update equity state, and maintain the index.
Runtime boundary — Exact feasibility checks remain part of the measured repair process.
